title: Digital Provenance Passport
summary: A research prototype agent that traces the provenance of artworks and artifacts, flags looting and repatriation risk, and issues a signed, tamper-evident passport for each object.

contribution.roleNote: Masters research at the NYU Center for Global Affairs under the Ethical Tech CoLab, built for the Microsoft × Coinbase x402 hackathon.

narrative.problem: Provenance for many objects is incomplete or contested, and the registers that certify stolen cultural property have no public API. Material taken from archaeological sites or under colonial rule was never reported stolen, so it cannot appear in a stolen-property register at all.
narrative.decision: Grounding searches an allowlist of authoritative sources and extracts only cited facts, so a claim with no source is never produced; no register check can return "clear", and every check, including failed ones, is signed into the Passport with its caveat.
narrative.tradeoff: The sourcing rule blocks unsourced claims, not false ones, and the allowlist of mostly Western institutions searches best where objects are already well documented and worst for source-country, colonial-era and archaeological material.
narrative.limitation: None of the fifteen catalogue scores was computed by the pipeline; each was assigned by hand. The web pipeline and the canonical scorer still return different numbers, and the national heritage authorities of source countries are not covered.
narrative.caveat: A research prototype for academic demonstration: outputs are indicative, not a determination of title. The published site is a pre-rendered capture whose passports are signed with a throwaway key; payments use the Base Sepolia testnet.
